Frozen Peanut Butter Bars

Molly Allen
Molly Allen

Micki WagnerShopping Writer

These easy frozen peanut butter bars combine a chocolate cookie crust with a fluffy peanut butter filing for a simple no-bake treat everyone will love.

Serves12 to 16

Prep40 minutes

Cook Mode+
Jump to Recipe

Quick Overview

Why You’ll Love Our Frozen Peanut Butter Bars

  • There are minimal ingredients. This recipe comes together with a handful of simple ingredients. Aside from the (optional) candy topping, you might already have them all!
  • Easy to make ahead. Prep these bars ahead of time and have them ready in the freezer to pull out anytime.

I’m a peanut butter and chocolate lover through and through, and this easy no-bake dessert recipe makes that flavor combination shine. These frozen peanut butter bars couldn’t be simpler. All you have to do is prep a quick Oreo cookie crust. Then, make homemade whipped cream and beat together cream cheese, peanut butter, powdered sugar, and vanilla. With whipped cream folded into the filling, it’s super-fluffy, flavorful, and not too sweet. Once the filling is spread over the crust, freeze the bars until set, and then dig in anytime. It’s the ideal refreshing treat to have waiting for you in the freezer on a warm day. Low effort meets maximum flavor, and I’m here for it.

Straight from Our Recipe Tester

“Peanut butter + Oreos + cream cheese = one dreamy dessert. How could it not? I absolutely love how fluffy the sweet, salty, tangy, rich peanut butter filling is. It goes perfectly with the crunchy, slightly bitter, slightly sweet, and totally chocolaty Oreo crumb base. And then you top it with crushed-up Reese’s cups? Please meet my new dream dessert.” —Micki, June 2026

Why You Should Trust Me

I’m a former bakery owner with 10-plus years of recipe development experience. I’m constantly thinking about desserts (baked in the oven or otherwise). I love simple no-bake desserts like this easy-to-prep treat for a crowd. 

Key Ingredients in Frozen Peanut Butter Bars

  • Peanut butter: Peanut butter is the star of the show, infusing the filling with flavor and making the ideal pairing for the chocolate cookie crust. Use creamy, no-stir peanut butter for the best texture.
  • Cream cheese: Cream cheese provides structure for the filling. It’s important to let it come to room temperature — softened cream cheese will incorporate better for the smoothest filling.
  • Oreos: Make a quick and easy cookie crust with this nostalgic favorite. Whole cookies are pulsed in a food processor to form crumbs and then mixed with melted butter.  
  • Peanut butter cups: This is an optional garnish, but it’s a great addition. Dress up the top of your peanut butter bars with chopped Reese’s, or any other favorite brand of peanut butter cups. Other options? Sprinkle mini chocolate chips over top, try it with peanut butter chips, or go for a drizzle of melted chocolate.

How to Make Frozen Peanut Butter Bars

  1. Prep the pan. Lightly coat an 8×8-inch square baking pan with cooking spray and line the pan with 2 sheets of parchment paper to form a sling.
  2. Make the crust. Process Oreo cookies in a food processor until fine crumbs form. Drizzle in melted unsalted butter and pulse until evenly moistened. Transfer the crumbs to the baking pan and use the bottom of a flat measuring cup or your hands to firmly press it into an even layer. Leave the crust in the freezer while making the filling.
  3. Make the filling. Beat cold heavy cream in a stand mixer with the whisk attachment on medium speed until firm peaks form, then transfer to another bowl. Beat room-temperature cream cheese and peanut butter together in a stand mixer. Beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla extract. Fold in the whipped cream.
  4. Assemble and freeze. Transfer the filling to the crust and spread into an even layer. Garnish with coarsely chopped Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups if desired. Cover and freeze until set, at least 4 hours or up to overnight. Once set, let the bars sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before cutting and serving.

Storage and Make-Ahead Tips

Freeze covered or in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

Frozen Peanut Butter Bars Recipe

These easy frozen peanut butter bars combine a chocolate cookie crust with a fluffy peanut butter filing for a simple no-bake treat everyone will love.

Prep time 40 minutes

Serves 12 to 16

Nutritional Info

  • tree-nut-free
  • fish-free
  • red-meat-free
  • pescatarian
  • pork-free
  • shellfish-free
  • vegetarian
  • alcohol-free
Per serving, based on 14 servings. (% daily value)
  • Calories 579
  • Fat 42.1 g (53.9%)
  • Saturated 18.3 g (78.0%)
  • Carbs 45.5 g (15.5%)
  • Fiber 2.3 g (6.1%)
  • Sugars 34.9 g
  • Protein 9.4 g (8.0%)
  • Sodium 221.3 mg (14.8%)

Ingredients

For the crust

  • Cooking spray

  • 22

    Oreo sandwich cookies (about 9 ounces)

  • 5 tablespoons

    unsalted butter, melted

For the filling

  • 8 ounces

    cream cheese, at room temperature

  • 1 3/4 cups

    cold heavy cream

  • 1 cup

    creamy peanut butter (not natural)

  • 1 1/2 cups

    powdered sugar

  • 2 teaspoons

    vanilla extract

  • 4

    regular-sized Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups, coarsely chopped (optional)

Instructions

Make the crust:

  1. Lightly coat an 8x8-inch square baking pan (at least 2 inches high) with cooking spray. Line the pan with 2 sheets of parchment paper, positioning them perpendicular to each other, so that the parchment hangs about 2 inches over all 4 sides of the pan to form a sling.

  2. Process 22 Oreo cookies in a food processor until fine crumbs form, 30 to 60 seconds. Drizzle in 5 tablespoons melted unsalted butter and pulse until evenly moistened, about 5 (1-second) pulses. (Alternatively, place the cookies in a re-sealable plastic bag and crush with a rolling pin into fine crumbs. Transfer to a medium bowl and stir in the butter.)

  3. Transfer to the baking pan and use the bottom of a flat measuring cup or your hands to firmly press it into an even layer. Freeze for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, make the filling.

Make the filling:

  1. Beat 1 3/4 cups cold heavy cream in a stand mixer with the whisk attachment on medium speed until firm peaks form, 5 to 8 minutes. Transfer to another bowl.

  2. Beat 8 ounces room-temperature cream cheese and 1 cup creamy peanut butter together in the stand mixer (no need to clean) with the paddle attachment on low speed until smooth, 10 to 20 seconds. Gradually beat in the 1 1/2 cups powdered sugar until combined, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed. Beat in 2 teaspoons vanilla extract.

  3. Working in two increments, fold the whipped cream into the peanut butter mixture with a flexible spatula just until combined and no streaks remain.

  4. Transfer to the crust and spread into an even layer. Garnish with 4 coarsely chopped Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups if desired.

  5. Cover and freeze until set, at least 4 hours or up to overnight. Grasping the excess parchment, lift the slab out of the pan and place on a cutting board. Let sit at room temperature for 15 minutes. Cut into 12 or 16 pieces, wiping the knife clean between each cut for the cleanest-looking slices.

Recipe Notes

Storage: Freeze in an airtight container for up to 1 week.
